title: EGY-11 · Telling: anecdotes, unexpected and reported discourse

blocks.text: EGY-11 · Telling: anecdotes, unexpected and discourse
reported
Lesson overview

With Layer B2 The Egyptian track passes from the phrases of everyday life to long conversation. The first step is the story: in Egypt, telling is an art, and a well-told story (ḥikāya) has a precise rhythm, with an attack, suspense, surprise, and a listener who reacts to every joke. In this unit learn the signs of the story (fi l-awwil, wi fagʾa, the-muhimm), the times of the past that serve to tell (kunt ba-..., kunt ḥa-..., kunt lissa...), the listener's reactions (lā yā šēḫ!, ya ḫabar!) and the speech reported in Egyptian: what he said, what he asked, what he said to do. Nine weeks, in parallel with B2-01, B2-02 and B2-03.

rows: 12–13 9 weeks (weeks) 157–165), about 1,5 hours per week in two blocks

blocks.text: Materials This unit, a tutor or an Egyptian conversation partner, video or story podcast in Egyptian (Appendix C)
Targets. At the end of the unit you know:
1. tell Egyptian an episode of 2–3 minutes with a clear order and a little suspense;
2. use the time of the story: past, progressive past (kunt ba-), ḥa-), I had a.
3. react to a story like an Egyptian listener;
4. report what someone has said, asked or ordered (ʾāl inn... saʾal Law... ʾalli aʿmil…);
5. follow an authentic recorded tale and summarize it.
Nine-week plan (two blocks from 40–45 minutes per week).

1. Dialogue 1 · The lost suitcase
Milan, September. Yāsmīn, the sister of ŠarīfShe's been here three days for her master's degree at the Polytechnic. Dinner by ŠarīfLuca asks her how the trip went.

2. The Signs of the Story
An Egyptian tale has a frame of fixed words: it is as learned as if they were the punctuation of history.

5. Dialogue 2 · What the chief said
A week later. Šarīf Go home from work and tell Luca about a meeting with his boss.

blocks.text: No timing. In Egyptian the verb reported remains as it was: ʾalli inn iš-šanṭa lissa fi l-ʾAhira "He told me that the suitcase was still in Cairo" (Lett. It's still in the air. In Italian we make the concordance. The order reported. After ʾāl or ʾalli + person, the verb goes to the imperfect without bi-: ʾalli astana ʾalha tīgi bukra łle said to come tomorrow. You often hear the direct phrase: ʾalli . tiʾlaʾš"Don't worry," he said. The forms of ʾāl + there. ʾalli (to me) · ʾallak · ʾallik (a te m./f.) · ʾallu (to him) · ʾalha (to you) · ʾallina (to us) · ʾallukum (to you) · ʾalluhum (to them). With other subjects: ʾultillu I told him, ʾalitli "She said to me, ʾalūli They told me.

8. Listening to an Authentic Story

What to choose. Personal stories recorded in Egyptian: short videos in which someone tells an episode (a trip, a job interview, a bad figure), conversation podcasts, interviews in which the guest remembers his own story. Choose recordings of 3–5 minutes, better with Arabic subtitles. See Appendix C. The method for a story.
1. Listen to everything once. Who tells, what happened to him, how does it end? Write three words.
2. Find the bones. Listen to and mark the signs of the story (section 2): where does the surprise begin? where Cut?
3. Find the voices. It marks every time the person who tells reports another's words (ʾalli, ʾultillu, saʾalni): who says What?
4. Tell it again. You're supposed to be in Egyptian in a minute, like it happened to a friend: ṣāḥbi ḥaṣallu
ḥāga…
9. Pronunciation

He suspense her. Before the surprise the voice slows down and lowers: wi ana wāʾfa… fiḍilt wāʾfa... wi fagʾa! And then fagʾa Take a little break. Exercises on Dialogue 1 With the tutor. The forms of ʾāl. ʾalli, ʾallu, ʾultillu they are pronounced as one word, with the accent on the first syllable: ʾÁlli, ʾÚltillu. The ʾ initial is the qāf cairota: don't pronounce it like a q.

13. Oral production

1. My misadventure (session). Tell the tutor, in 2–3 minutes, an unexpected that happened to you (a travel, a lost document, a misunderstanding). Use section signals 2, at least two times in the section 3 and two sentences reported. The tutor reacts as in the section 4; Then reverse the roles.
2. The wireless phone. The tutor tells you three sentences (information, a question, an order); You refer them to a Third with the speech reported.
3. The voicemail. Record a one-minute voice message, like Umm Šarīf, where you tell a Egyptian friend a conversation you had.
